formula: Do not get me wrong, but + complete clause

formulas.formula: Do not get me wrong, but + complete clause

example: Do not get me wrong, but enthusiasm alone is not enough.
exampleZh: 不要誤會我的意思，但單靠熱誠並不足夠。

examples.en: Do not get me wrong, but enthusiasm alone is not enough.
examples.zh: 不要誤會我的意思，但單靠熱誠並不足夠。
examples.highlight: Do not get me wrong, but enthusiasm alone is not enough.

rules.zh: 在 Do not get me wrong, but 後面，內容必須是完整子句，即同時有主語和限定動詞。只有 too expensive 之類的形容詞片語並不足以構成完整子句。
rules.en: Use a complete clause after but Do not get me wrong, but the plan needs more work. “the plan needs more work” Do not get me wrong, but too expensive. “too expensive”

rules.zh: 它通常不是用來完全收回前面的正面評價，而是補充一項限制或不同意見。
rules.en: The expression normally introduces a qualification I like the design. However, it is difficult to use. Do not get me wrong, but the design is difficult to use even though I like it.

rules.zh: 除非前文可能令人誤解說話者對其兄弟或足球的看法，否則這句缺乏清楚的溝通目的。
rules.en: Do not use it before a completely unrelated idea Unnatural: Do not get me wrong, but my brother plays football.

rules.zh: 在日常對話中十分常見。本練習統一使用完整形式：【Do not get me wrong, but...】
rules.en: The full form is required in this exercise The contraction Don’t get me wrong is common in conversation. “Don’t get me wrong” However, this exercise consistently practises: Do not get me wrong, but... Do not get me wrong, but...

rules.zh: 在 wrong 後使用逗號。當句型出現在直接引語內，需要使用引號。
rules.en: Punctuation When the expression begins the sentence, place a comma after wrong: Do not get me wrong, but I understand your concern. When it appears inside direct speech, use quotation marks: The coach said, “Do not get me wrong, but the players made several mistakes.”

rules.zh: 這個句型適合在可能出現誤會時使用，但不應在每次提出不同意見時都使用。過度使用可能令人覺得說話者過於防衛。
rules.en: It can sound defensive if it is overused

benefits.zh: 這個句型提醒聽者，不要把你接下來的意見理解成完全否定、攻擊或拒絕。
benefits.en: It prevents unnecessary misunderstanding This structure tells the listener that your next comment should not be taken as a completely negative opinion.

benefits.zh: 你不需要一開始便直接批評對方，而可以先表明自己的立場並非完全負面。比較：你的計劃行不通。不要誤會我的意思，但我認為這個計劃以目前的形式並不可行。第二句聽起來較有分寸，也清楚顯示說話者正在評論計劃，而不一定是在攻擊提出計劃的人。
benefits.en: It helps you disagree without sounding immediately hostile Instead of beginning directly with a criticism, you can first show that your position is more balanced. Compare: Your plan will not work. Do not get me wrong, but I do not think the plan will work in its present form.

benefits.zh: 你可以先承認某項優點，再提出限制或憂慮。不要誤會我的意思，但這個構思雖然有創意，卻太昂貴。
benefits.en: It allows you to recognise a good point before adding a concern You can acknowledge something positive and then explain its limitation. Do not get me wrong, but although the idea is creative, it is too expensive.

benefits.zh: 聽者可以明白你的看法並不是單純的「支持」或「反對」，而是包含條件、限制或保留。
benefits.en: It makes your real position clearer The listener can understand that your opinion contains more than a simple yes or no.

benefits.zh: 這個句型可以作為現成的口語框架，讓你在說話時更有條理地提出不同意見或批評。
benefits.en: It is a useful speaking frame The expression gives you time to organise a careful disagreement or criticism while speaking.
